{{Top|ca|leg}}
{{Quote|<nowiki />''[The Priapulin]'' even tell time in terms of the tidal shifts of their world; one tidal hour equals ten galactic standard hours.|Mammon Hoole, ''The Essential Guide to Alien Species''|<ref name="TEGAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref>}}
'''Tidal hours''' were a unit of [[Time/Legends|time]] used by the [[Water/Legends|aquatic]] [[Priapulin]] [[Species/Legends|species]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Pria/Legends|Pria]] that were based on the tidal shifts of Pria's [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]]. By the time of the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]],<ref name="Sanbra">{{GamerCite|8|The University of Sanbra Guide to Intelligent Life: The Priapulin}}</ref> which began in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> tidal hours had been equivalent to ten [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]] for several [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] as a result of the so-called "perfect [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]]" of [[Pria's sole moon]]. Because of this conversion factor, the Pria referred to a standard hour as a "tenth of a tide" and termed a period of five standard hours a "half-tide."<ref name="Sanbra" /> At some point during the reign of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]], [[Sentientologist|Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] mentioned tidal hours in his book ''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''.<ref name="TEGAS" />

==Behind the scenes==
Tidal hours were first mentioned in the [[2001]] reference book [[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']], written by [[Ann Margaret Lewis]] and published as part of the ''[[Star Wars: Essential Guides]]'' series.<ref name="TEGAS" />
